<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **60** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/mcp/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via os skills install (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/skills/install.ts))_
- `content/docs/ai/skills.mdx`  _(via os skills install (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/skills/install.ts), os skills status (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/skills/status.ts), os skills update (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/skills/update.ts))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via expectedVersion (symbol, a field of interface SkillsStatusReport))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via expectedVersion (symbol, a field of interface SkillsStatusReport))_
- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via installedVersion (symbol, a field of interface SkillsStatusReport))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via installedVersion (symbol, a field of interface SkillsStatusReport), os skills install (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/skills/install.ts), os skills status (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/skills/status.ts), os skills update (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/skills/update.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via expectedVersion (symbol, a field of interface SkillsStatusReport))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via expectedVersion (symbol, a field of interface SkillsStatusReport))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/mcp/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **23** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d5a045a501cbdcb182c48bc76b661e5c725b19a2` — the merge of head `bbb4b559c725123927de8e0950ec5ecb77f49d97` into base `301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d5a045a501cbdcb182c48bc76b661e5c725b19a2 && git checkout d5a045a501cbdcb182c48bc76b661e5c725b19a2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d bbb4b559c725123927de8e0950ec5ecb77f49d97 && git checkout -B drift-repro 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d && git merge --no-ff bbb4b559c725123927de8e0950ec5ecb77f49d97

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-18T01:43Z

Head-sha: 3dcccc78268eaa6a95f1452b01963c55fb946079
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34773 (claim 6963642503, os-dev report 6966410576).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #34773`, base `main`. The head is a `main` merge on top of `bec9bdc5`. Fifteen paths, +1505/-13:
- the new `os skills` group: three commands, three utils, the topic in `package.json`, and a 399-line test;
- the MCP `initialize` install line, with its pin and README;
- three docs pages;
- a changeset.

Not governed. `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/mcp` are at `patch`, and `Metadata-protocol: none` keeps them there. `Clause-②: yes (widening: a new published CLI command group)` is right.

**CI.** Green on this head: 41 success, 15 expected skips.

**(1) The overlap-check exit 1.** The one conflict is #34791 against `main` at `cli.mdx:890`, as o3-G says. It is not in this diff. At `bec9bdc5` it was clean. Nothing is owed here. Whichever of the two lands second resolves that hunk.

**(2) Body readings at `bec9bdc5`.** The merge brings only `main` in, and the report carries the merged head's readings, so the body's readings stand.

**The version source.** `--version` must be exact semver, with no range or tag. `--target` reads `versions.skills` through `loadRestrictionProfile`, the reader `os validate --target` uses, and refuses a value that is not exact. Without either, the CLI's own version is used. I checked that `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/skills` and `@objectstack/mcp` all sit in `.changeset/config.json`'s one `fixed` group, so that default names the catalog released with the CLI. `--version` and `--target` are mutually exclusive, and the output says which source it used.

**The catalog.** `npm pack @objectstack/skills@V`, run in the cwd, so `.npmrc`, scope mapping, auth and proxy apply. It goes through `execFile` with arguments, with a shell only on Windows for the `.cmd` shim. The result is unpacked in process:
- every header's checksum is checked;
- pax `path` and GNU long names are honoured;
- the package must declare `@objectstack/skills` at exactly V;
- only `package/dist/skills/<name>/**` is kept, for a `<name>` that holds `SKILL.md`;
- an empty, `.` or `..` segment, or a link or any non-regular type, is refused;
- the skill name must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`;
- a version the registry lacks (`ETARGET` or `E404`) is refused, naming it.

**Ownership.** `.objectstack-skills.json` records the version and a SHA-256 for every file.
- `install` over a record is refused, pointing to `update`. A same-named directory it did not write is refused unless `--force`, which reports it as adopted.
- `update` with no record is refused, pointing to `install`. A locally modified catalog skill is refused unless `--force`. A new catalog skill that collides with one of the user's own directories is refused even with `--force`.
- Only the planned directories are touched, and the record is written last.
- A malformed record is refused whole, so a half-read record never lets `update` touch skills it did not write. Recorded names with `/`, `\`, or a leading `.` are refused, and `..` with them.

**Status.** It reports the installed and expected versions, plus missing, modified and extra skills. Only a version mismatch, a missing skill or a modified skill is a mismatch. It exits 0, or 1 with `--check`. The registry is not read.

**The MCP line.** `initialize` now names `os skills install --version V`, with `npx -p @objectstack/cli@V os skills install --version V` as the form for a machine without the CLI. The CLI's `bin` declares `os`, so the `npx -p` form resolves. The changeset says it supersedes the `pnpm add -D` line in the same release. The order said `/mcp/skill` also carries this line, and it does not. That is the correct reading of the code, not a gap.

**Tests and evidence.** Twenty-two cases, including the Done-when end to end (install in an empty directory, then status reports a mismatch after the server moves) and every refusal above. The MCP pin was red first. The two ablation legs are ownership and status mismatch. The live registry run is in the report.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. The unpacker's "path outside its own tree" check holds only for `/`-separated segments.** `catalogFromTarball` splits on `/` and refuses `''`, `.` and `..`. A segment such as `..\..\x` or `C:x` passes. On Windows, `applySkillsWrite`'s `join(root, ...path.split('/'))` then treats the `\` as a separator, and the write leaves the skills directory. `npm pack` never writes such a name, but the check exists for a tarball that is not what it claims, and the module header promises that guarantee on every platform. Please refuse a segment containing `\` or `:` as well, or check that the joined target resolves under `root` before writing. Add one case to "refuses a link and a path that leaves its tree" for the backslash form.

### Notes
- N1. The branch carries a commit titled `wip(cli): …` (`7dea998c`). The landing squashes it, so nothing is owed. If the queue keeps history, that subject should be reworded first.
- N2. `update` with no `--version` or `--target` moves the catalog to the CLI's own version, not to a target's. That is consistent with `install`, and the output names the source. A user who upgraded the server but not the CLI needs `--target`, and the docs page shows it.

Next: S1, a small code change that gets a delta read. Then the seat's opus L2 for the Clause-② declaration, then o3-G lands.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3dcccc78268eaa6a95f1452b01963c55fb946079`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. The PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening …)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. No published schema and no governed path is in the 15-path tree. The guard on the head reports `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, and the dev's check-governed-merges reading is 0 of 15.
Inputs: card #34773 (body, triage 6963599108, claim 6963642503, os-dev report 6966410576); PR #35060 (body, the docs-drift advisory 6965683534, L1-c ACCEPT 6966450600, contract-review claim 6966470586; no reviews or inline comments); the net diff `eb7b09d4..3dcccc78` (+1505/-13); and the check-runs on the head: 41 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. Check Changeset, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint & Repo Gates, all ten Test Core shards, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links and the Type Check jobs are all success. The skips are UI, opt-in and queue jobs, skipped by filter.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **New CLI topic `skills`, with `install`, `update` and `status`. Right.** The topic is in `packages/cli/package.json` `oclif.topics`. The commands are `packages/cli/src/commands/skills/{install,status,update}.ts`, and they are purely additive. No existing command, flag, alias or topic is removed or renamed: the only `package.json` hunk is the 3-line topic insertion.
2. **New flags. Right.** All three commands take `--version`, `--target`, `--dir` and `--json`. `install` and `update` also take `--force`, and `status` takes `--check`. `--version` and `--target` are mutually `exclusive`. A subcommand-level `version` string flag has precedent (`package install`, `package publish`), and oclif reads `--version` as its own version flag only in argv position 0, so `os skills install --version X` parses as the command's flag.
3. **New exit-code and `--json` contracts. Right, and they match the docs.**
   - Every refusal exits 1 with `{ ok: false, command, error }` on stdout under `--json`.
   - `status` exits 0, or exits 1 when `--check` is given and there is a mismatch. A mismatch is no record, a different version, or a missing or modified skill. Extra skills are not a mismatch.
   - The `SkillsStatusReport` and `SkillsWriteResult` shapes are new output, not a change to existing output.
4. **New on-disk state, `.objectstack-skills.json` in the skills dir. Right in design.**
   - The record holds the package, an exact version, and every file with its sha256.
   - It is written last. A malformed record is refused whole. `install` over an existing record is refused and points to `update`. `update` with no record is refused and points to `install`.
   - Ownership: `update` never writes into a directory the record does not name, and a new catalog skill that collides with such a directory is refused even with `--force`. `install --force` adopts same-named directories and names them as adopted.
   - Idempotency: `install` is deliberately non-repeatable, and `update` to the same version is a clean re-write.
   - One gap in the record's validation is in ③, S2.
5. **Network source and failure modes. Right.**
   - The catalog is fetched with `npm pack @objectstack/skills@V`, run in the cwd, so the user's `.npmrc` and `npm_config_*` settings apply. The timeout is 120 s and the buffer 16 MB.
   - `ENOENT` gets a "no npm on PATH" sentence. `ETARGET` and `E404` are refused as unpublished, naming the version. Any other error passes npm's summary through.
   - The tarball must declare `@objectstack/skills` at exactly V, its checksums must hold, and links and non-regular types are refused. Only `dist/skills/NAME/**` with a `SKILL.md` is kept.
   - V must match the exact-semver regex before it reaches the argv or a shell, so no shell injection is possible through the version, whether it comes from `--version` or from a target profile.
   - One Windows-only argv defect is in ③, S3.
6. **MCP: `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`. Right: the served tool surface is unchanged.**
   - The only hunk is the body of `skillsInstallLine()`, which is the prose of the open HTTP server's `initialize` `result.instructions`.
   - No tool, tool field, input schema or `tools/list` entry is added or removed.
   - The replaced `pnpm add -D` wording comes from #34686, whose changeset (`.changeset/34686-initialize-selection-rule.md`) is still pending on `main`. `@objectstack/mcp` is at 18.5.0, so no released text is narrowed.
   - The pin test drops the old `@objectstack/skills@V` assertion and adds `os skills install --version V`, the `npx -p @objectstack/cli@V` form, and a check that `pnpm add` is absent.
7. **Docs against the code. Right.**
   - `cli.mdx` `### Skills`: the version order, the npm-pack source, the record, the refusals, the `--force` semantics on each command, the status buckets and the mismatch rule, the exit codes, and every flags-table row match the code.
   - `skills.mdx`: the three commands, `--force` as the migration from `experimental_sync`, and update's ownership rule match.
   - `connect-mcp.mdx` and `packages/mcp/README.md` quote the new `initialize` line as the runtime emits it.
   - The overlap-check exit 1 is confirmed not to be this PR's. #34791 (head `790dd2ba`) edits `cli.mdx:890`, changing `Running author-time rules (70)` to `(69)`, while `main` reads `(71)` there. This diff touches `cli.mdx` only at the `@@ -3672 +3672` insertion. It is not charged here.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/cli: patch` and `@objectstack/mcp: patch` are correct.** AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist step 3, and the level axis of `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (ruling A, #25105), make the level follow the metadata protocol alone. `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". A new published CLI command group moves no authorable metadata, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right and `patch` is what the gate requires. Check Changeset is success on the head.
- Both packages sit in the one `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json`, with `@objectstack/skills`. `packages/skills` is not moved, and needs no entry.
- **Clause-②: yes (widening) is correct.** The diff adds a published CLI group, its flags, its exit and JSON contracts, and a state file. It removes or renames no CLI command or flag, no MCP tool, and no tool field. The `initialize` prose swap replaces an unreleased line, so it is not a narrowing. The line is identical in the PR body and in the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's `open_questions` is `[]`, and `security_findings` is "none". Each out-of-scope note is answered:

- `--target` against an open `os dev` is refused with the reader's existing 404, because the restriction-profile route is cloud-only. This is the existing behaviour of `loadRestrictionProfile`. The MCP line carries `--version V` for open servers, so it is accepted as noted.
- `/mcp/skill` carries no install line. Confirmed: `skillsInstallLine` is the only source. This is a correct reading of the code.
- `skills-reference.mdx` and `packages/skills/README.md` still lead with the `pnpm add` path. That path still works. They belong to the skills lane and are not owed here.
- #34791's `cli.mdx:890` conflict is confirmed in ① item 7.

SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): not applicable. The diff is CLI filesystem and registry I/O plus MCP prose. There is no id materialisation, no query, and no in-app join.

Must-fix: none.

Should-fix:

- **S1. Open, carried by its L1 name, and I agree.** `catalogFromTarball` splits on `/` only. A segment such as `..\..\x` or `C:x` passes, and on Windows `applySkillsWrite`'s `join(root, ...path.split('/'))` then writes outside the skills dir. The fix the dev has announced covers this catalog-to-write path, and also NTFS alternate streams (`SKILL.md:x`): refuse `\` and `:` in a segment, and check that the resolved path is contained in the skills dir. It lands on a later head.
- **S2 (new; S1's fix does not cover it).** An empty skill name in the record deletes the whole skills directory.
  - `readSkillsManifest` refuses a recorded name containing `/` or `\`, or one starting with `.`, but it accepts `""`.
  - In `update`, `planSkillsWrite` marks `""` as dropped, because no catalog has it. `applySkillsWrite` then runs `rmSync(join(dir, ""), { recursive: true })`, which is `rmSync(dir)`. That wipes `.claude/skills/` itself, including every user-owned skill, before it re-writes the catalog.
  - Without `--force` the same record shows up as a modified skill and is refused. With `--force`, which the docs and refusal text offer as "discard local changes to catalog skills", it deletes skills the tool never installed. That breaks the ownership guarantee the changeset, the docs and the code comments promise.
  - The record is a file inside the repository, so a hand-edited or committed record is enough to trigger it.
  - Fix: validate recorded names with the catalog's own `SKILL_NAME` regex, `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`. Ideally, also validate recorded file paths with S1's segment rule; today those are only read, and only after `listFiles` has seen them. Add a malformed-record case to the tests.
- **S3 (new; Windows only).** `npm pack` with `shell: true` breaks when the temp path contains a space.
  - On Windows, `skillsRegistry.fetchTarball` runs `execFile('npm', [..., '--pack-destination', destination, ...], { shell: true })`. With `shell`, Node joins the argv with spaces and does no quoting. A `%TEMP%` under a user profile with a space, such as `C:\Users\First Last\AppData\Local\Temp`, splits `--pack-destination`. npm then reads the tail as a second pack spec, and the install fails with an unrelated npm error.
  - The version is regex-guarded, so this is a functional defect, not an injection.
  - Fix: quote `destination` when `shell` is set, or keep the cwd for `.npmrc` resolution and pass a destination without spaces. Pin it with a unit test on the argv the seam builds.

Nits:

- **N1.** The pending #34686 changeset still says "with its `pnpm add -D` command". Both entries will compile into the same release's `CHANGELOG.md`, and a reader who greps `pnpm add` lands on the stale sentence. It would be cleaner to amend that pending line in this PR than to rely on a superseding sentence.
- **N2.** `applySkillsWrite` is not transactional. An I/O failure mid-write leaves catalog directories removed under the old record, and an aborted `update` then needs `--force`. Staging in a sibling temp dir and renaming would make it atomic.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34773-os-skills-install`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: PASS**
